issues.description: The solution inconsistently treats the symbol display_start as memory contents in set_pixel (using add eax, [display_start]) while elsewhere (main) it is used as an address (mov esi, display_start). The template defines display_start as a BSS label (RESB), i.e. a block of memory whose address should be used as the framebuffer base. Using [display_start] dereferences that memory and adds whatever (uninitialized) bytes are stored there instead of adding the base address, causing incorrect address computation and wrong writes. This mismatch between treating display_start as an address vs. as stored data is an unintentional structural bug that will confuse students and lead to incorrect behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Treat display_start consistently as the base address (label) rather than memory contents. In set_pixel replace 'add eax, [display_start]' with adding the label address (e.g. 'add eax, display_start') or load the base into a register first ('mov esi, display_start' and then 'add esi, eax' and write 'mov [esi], ecx'). Ensure all uses across main and set_pixel use the label address form.
